chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a man, between me and him was a relationship, who died and left young children, and left slaves for him, boys and girls, and did not make a bequest. So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them to serve as the mother of his child, and what is your view regarding their sale? He said: 'If there is a guardian for them who manages their affairs, sells them on their behalf, and looks out for their interests, he is rewarded in doing so.' I said, 'So what is your view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, so he takes her as the mother of his child?' He said: 'There is no problem with that, if that evaluation is established for them by the supervisor with regards to what is correct for them, and there is not for them to retract with regards to what the supervisor establishes for them with regards to what is right for them.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (a female slave who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling slave children left by an intestate father, and can a buyer take one as a mother of a child?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of intestate succession regarding slave children, emphasizing the guardian's (wali) fiduciary duty to act in their best interest during the sale of their personhood. It specifically validates the status of 'Umm Walad' acquired through such a sale, establishing that the children cannot later contest the transaction once the guardian has executed it properly, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the finality of the wali's administrative decisions in estate management.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a man, between me and him was a relationship, died and left young children, and left slaves for him, boys and girls, and did not make a bequest. So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them to serve the mother of his children, and what is your<sup>asws</sup> view with regards to selling them?’ 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If there is a guardian for them, they would be evaluated by his order to be sold over them, and with having consideration for them if there were ones who were paid among them’. I said, ‘So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding the one who buys the slave girl from them, so he takes her for the mother of his child?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with that, if that evaluation is established for them by the supervisor with regards to what is correct for them (young inheritors), and there is not for them to retract with regards to what evaluation the supervisors establishes for them with regards to what is right for them’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man with whom I have a relation of kinship, he dies leaving behind small children, slaves and slave-girls but has not made any will. ‘What do you say about buying a slave-girl for a mother of one’s child and what do you say about selling them?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If they have a guardian who supervises for them the sale and looks after them, he will receive good rewards.’ I asked, ‘What do you say about one’s buying from them a slave- girl for a mother of one’s child?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if it is executed by their guardian who looks after their interests and well-being; and they cannot change their mind about what the guardian has done for them who looks after their well-being.’”
